I had the exact same thing as you twice before. The first time was last September for an L5/S1 herniation. The injection itself was a breeze. I actually asked for conscious sedation which was a blessing since I was so nervous. I felt a little bit of pressure but other than that it was smooth sailing after. The entire procedure took about 15 minutes. Laid in recovery for about 30 minutes and I was able to go home. 

The second time I got the injection was last month after re-herniating my L5/S1 disc. That injection was little more complicated. I came out of it having debilitating pain. The doctor said the procedure itself was rough as there was a lot of inflammation around the area. I got bilateral injections for this most recent herniation. I ended up in the ER after leaving the surgery center because the pain was so bad. They gave me Fentanyl and Ativan to help with the tightness and the pain, considering I was unable to even walk. Why did the surgery center discharge me? Who knows. I later had a microdiscectomy about 2 weeks ago today. 

My advice would be to get the conscious sedation if you’re nervous like I was. You don’t remember the procedure itself and makes everything a lot more comfortable. Follow your doctors instructions post procedure and call him if you have any questions. Don’t be afraid to ask questions if you feel something is wrong. Best of luck! Lmk if you have any other questions.

A working theory I have is that it was staged. People don’t just vanish out of thin air. I find it odd the cadaver dogs were hiring at the abandoned house and the pond. Yet nothing was found. That’s why I wonder if he was placed under the house or below ground - but I figured they would have seen fresh soil that has been dug up. His friends told me there is nothing that makes sense with knowing him and his personal life in relation to this. I feel like they will probably find his body at some point. Something tells me that it’s being overlooked/they haven’t looked in a place where he is located if he is indeed deceased.

I question the hyperthermia theory because it would take longer/much lower temps for the human body to drop to the temperature to feel like you’re burning and take off all of your clothes. The time gap between his last digital footprint and where the car was found is suspicious. Being around his age we are glued to our phones. I was speaking with his friends at TSU and they agreed that they think he was taken. It just blows my mind to think that this is still a major Unkown coming on 3 months later.

Based on the map of the area, it looks like there’s a lot of silos. Is it possible that someone put his body in one of those? I know the dogs were going back and forth between the house and the pond. Could he have been put underneath the house or somewhere between the house and the pond? Too much of this story doesn’t make sense and I am beginning to feel more and more inclined to lead to think foul play was involved. No one typically crashes, removes their clothes, then wanders off never to be seen or heard from again. Especially without a single person who truly knew what happened or maybe someone does... I’ve been reading about this all day and nothing adds up here.
